subtitle: Strokes and time
unlocks: Explain why a person keeps a bad relationship, count strokes in a greeting, spot a pastime

levels.title: Spinal Cord
levels.playsLike: Spitz's infants, Levine's rats: the player runs a week with zero recognition and watches a mood meter fall; lesson: stroke hunger is biological

levels.title: Stroke Sorter
levels.playsLike: Lines fly in; drag each to positive/negative x conditional/unconditional; the twist round: "which of these would you accept?" (filter)

levels.title: Hi-Hi
levels.playsLike: Mr C returns from vacation; the player builds the greeting to pay the ~30 strokes owed; too few = offence, too many = "is he selling insurance?"

levels.title: The Party
levels.playsLike: Six corners of a cocktail party; identify each as ritual / pastime / activity / game / intimacy / withdrawal from 3 lines of overheard talk

levels.title: PTA Three Ways
levels.playsLike: Same pastime at P-P ("Juvenile Delinquency"), A-A ("PTA"), C-C levels; player matches the level

levels.title: The Stroke Economy
levels.playsLike: Steiner's five rules are the "laws" of a town; the player must break each one in a scene and feel the pushback; L3 argues why the rules exist (who benefits)

subtitle: Ego states
unlocks: Diagnose P/A/C from voice, words, posture; tell contamination from Adult

levels.title: Who Said That
levels.playsLike: A line, a tone, a posture: Parent, Adult or Child? Starts with easy archetypes, ends with mixed cues

levels.title: Five Faces
levels.playsLike: Functional model: CP / NP / A / FC / AC, each with a + and - side; the hard round shows negative NP (smothering) and positive CP (firm boundary)

levels.title: Egogram
levels.playsLike: Player draws their own egogram, then one for a character from a 10-line monologue; compares

levels.title: Four Ways to Know
levels.playsLike: Same ego-state call made from behaviour, from how others respond, from history, from the character's own sense; player must get 2 of 4 to agree

levels.title: Little Professor
levels.playsLike: Second-order structure: Mike (age 3) at the dinner table from GPP; player plays the father and decides whether to break the game in statu nascendi

levels.title: The Contaminated Adult
levels.playsLike: Ten "Adult" statements; some are Parent prejudice, some Child delusion, some double; L3 also flags exclusion

subtitle: Transactions
unlocks: Keep a conversation open, cross one on purpose, hear the ulterior level

levels.title: Draw the Arrow
levels.playsLike: Two PAC stacks; player drags stimulus and response arrows; checks complementarity

levels.title: Keep It Going
levels.playsLike: Pick the response that keeps a complementary chain alive for 6 turns - including an unhealthy P-C chain, to make the point

levels.title: Cross It
levels.playsLike: A Child-to-Parent whine arrives; player must cross it to reach Adult-Adult without starting Uproar; Karpman's options as the menu

levels.title: Why Did You Do That?
levels.playsLike: Berne's own group-therapy scene (ch.9, Figs. 7-8): Camellia and Rosita give the real Type I crossing, Mr. Troy gives the real Type II; player reproduces both

levels.title: The Barn
levels.playsLike: Duplex transaction: the player writes both the social line and the psychological line for each turn of the cowboy scene

levels.title: The Salesman
levels.playsLike: Angular transaction: "This one is better, but you can't afford it." Player must respond from Adult at both levels three times in a row

subtitle: Games
unlocks: Name the game from the switch, refuse to play, write the full analysis

levels.title: Is It a Game?
levels.playsLike: Pastime, operation, manoeuvre or game? The tell: a payoff after a switch

levels.title: Formula G
levels.playsLike: Scenes cut into 6 cards (Con, Gimmick, Response, Switch, Crossup, Payoff); order them; then tag which Drama Triangle role each player holds before and after the Switch

levels.title: Life Games
levels.playsLike: Alcoholic (5-handed: player cycles through Persecutor, Rescuer, Patsy, Connection), Debtor, Kick Me, NIGYSOB, SWYMD; each with the 6 advantages to fill at L3

levels.title: Home Games
levels.playsLike: Corner, Courtroom, Frigid Woman/Man, Harried, IWFY, LHHIT, Sweetheart; player must find the antithesis (e.g. "Yes, honey!" for Sweetheart; third-person ban for Courtroom)

levels.title: Room Games
levels.playsLike: Party, consulting-room, underworld and Good games; the Good-games round asks "what makes this one good?"

levels.title: Why Don't You-Yes But
levels.playsLike: The player is Black in a group of five; every suggestion gets a "Yes, but"; the only win is anti-ITHY: "That's a difficult problem. What are you going to do about it?" L3 writes the full GPP analysis

subtitle: Rackets, discounts, passivity
unlocks: Tell racket from real feeling, find the discount level, spot over-adaptation

levels.title: Real or Racket
levels.playsLike: Feeling shown; is it authentic (resolves the situation) or racket (substitutes, never resolves)?

levels.title: Stamp Book
levels.playsLike: Player watches a character collect grievances for a week and chooses the cash-in; lesson: stamps are the licence for the script payoff

levels.title: Four Levels
levels.playsLike: A problem statement; player climbs the Discount Matrix: is the existence, significance, changeability or personal ability being discounted?

levels.title: Doing Nothing
levels.playsLike: Four passive behaviours shown in an office; over-adaptation is the trap level

levels.title: Two Halves
levels.playsLike: A symbiosis: one person carries Parent+Adult, the other Child; player must find the move that lets both use all three

levels.title: The Discount Matrix
levels.playsLike: A six-scene conversation with redefinitions; player must name the discount level and the tangential/blocking move at each turn

subtitle: Scripts
unlocks: Draw a script matrix from a life story, hear a driver, name the injunction

levels.title: OK Corral
levels.playsLike: Place 12 inner statements on the OK Corral; then track one character's position across a day

levels.title: Hear the Driver
levels.playsLike: 5-second behaviour clips in text; name the driver from the words/gestures Kahler listed

levels.title: Don't
levels.playsLike: Childhood scenes, mostly nonverbal; name the injunction a child would decode; then the permission that counters it

levels.title: Three Banal Scripts
levels.playsLike: Steiner's Lovelessness, Mindlessness, Joylessness - play a day in each; the Pig Parent narrates

levels.title: Script Process
levels.playsLike: Until / After / Never / Always / Almost / Open-ended: match six life stories, then spot the player's own

levels.title: The Script Matrix
levels.playsLike: From a 25-line life story, drag injunctions, counter-injunctions and programme onto the matrix; L3 names the early decision and proposes a redecision

subtitle: Contracts, permission, intimacy
unlocks: Write a contract, give permission, decline a Rescue, sustain a game-free exchange

levels.title: Help or Rescue
levels.playsLike: Steiner's three Rescue rules; the player sorts 12 helping acts

levels.title: The Contract
levels.playsLike: Write a contract with a character; validator checks Berne's four requirements and Steiner's cooperative-contract clauses

levels.title: Three P's
levels.playsLike: Give permission only with protection and potency behind it; giving permission without protection fails the level

levels.title: Despair to Laughter
levels.playsLike: A game is refused; the player must hold the antithesis through the other player's escalation until "There I go again!"

levels.title: Awareness / Spontaneity / Intimacy
levels.playsLike: Three scenes (eating an orange, a crossed conversation, a candid one); player chooses the autonomous move, not the scripted one

levels.title: After Games, What?
levels.playsLike: Six-turn candid exchange with a character who keeps offering game openings; sustain intimacy without rescuing, persecuting or withdrawing; L3 writes a reflection graded by rubric
